title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
summary: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown.
card_summary: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown.
email_summary: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown. The same attack could be extended to reach the credentials Muse stores for the user's connected accounts.

title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
summary: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG.
card_summary: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG.

sections.technical:
The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0, A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions.

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-129975.

email_summary: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. Tracked as CVE-2026-129975.

title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
summary: Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week.
card_summary: Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week.

sections.impact:
The flaw allows an attacker with no account to write files outside the server's storage folder, and it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup,

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.

title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
summary: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com , a six year old Florida business that claimed to use advanced cryptographic tools to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

sections.overview: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com , a six year old Florida business that claimed to use advanced cryptographic tools to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.
sections.mitigation: The website RansomwareHelp urged victims Do not pay the ransom!, claiming its advanced cryptographic tools could restore 100 percent of data, servers, and systems to their original format, and that there was no need to give in to extortion demands. Ihme said RansomwareHelp sent a proposal to the victim with a recovery price of $438,880, which it claimed included professional configuration of forensic servers, expert engineering hours of programming to configure decryption algorithms, and eight (6-hour processing cycles) related to the decryption process. But Ihme said a review of the company s network at the time found only one copy of the ransom note, which was unearthed from a backup snapshot on one of the infected computers.
sections.context: This aligns with ongoing ransomware campaigns targeting operational continuity and recovery readiness.

email_summary: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com , a six year old Florida business that claimed to use advanced cryptographic tools to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed. Severity is rated high.
